key_insight: A transferred monolayer graphene contact improves nitride-based AlInN/Si solar-cell performance by boosting current collection and fill factor without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, semitransparent conductive contact that can enhance photovoltaic efficiency in nitride-on-silicon devices while remaining compatible with device fabrication constraints.
method: AlxIn1-xN solar cells were grown on p-type Si(100) with a thin amorphous-Si buffer layer to improve the heterointerface.
Three Al compositions were tested: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
A monolayer graphene film was transferred onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact layer.
evidence_signal: Devices with graphene were evaluated under illuminated and dark conditions, and the abstract reports higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency for all compositions, with little change in open-circuit voltage.
watch_item: The improvement is demonstrated for a specific set of AlInN compositions and a transfer-based graphene contact, so scalability, uniformity, and contact stability still need verification.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
